E-mail: rwilliams@yale.edu 18 04 2005 2 4 e124 e132 Smith et al. 2005 This is an open-access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License Background Caffeine is one of the most widely consumed psychoactive substances in the world. Methods and Findings We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of caffeine on human health. Conclusions Moderate caffeine consumption appears to have both beneficial and adverse health effects. caffeine meta-analysis systematic review human health Medicine Introduction Caffeine (1,3,7-trimethylxanthine) is a stimulant of the central nervous system. This review examines the evidence for both beneficial and adverse effects of caffeine consumption. Methods Search Strategy We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials. Selection Criteria We included randomized controlled trials and observational studies examining caffeine effects. Results We identified 47 studies meeting inclusion criteria. Table 1 Characteristics of Included Studies Summary of study design and population characteristics. Study Year Population Outcome Study A 2003 100 adults Increased alertness Study B 2004 50 subjects Sleep disruption Discussion Our findings suggest that caffeine has complex effects on human health. Low to moderate consumption may provide cognitive benefits 1 , while high doses may lead to adverse effects 2 . Conclusions Caffeine consumption should be tailored to individual tolerance and health status. Acknowledgments We thank all participants who contributed to this research. References Brown T Davis K Cognitive effects of caffeine J Neurosci 2002 15 234 241 Green M Adverse effects of high caffeine consumption Am J Health 2003 8 112 120 Supplementary Material 1 Additional data and statistical analyses
